## Applied Exercises

Work on these exercises in a copy of Charles River Reports.pbix, saved with **File > Save as** after you finish this chapter's tutorials, such as `Ch13 Exercises.pbix`. Build each exercise on its own report page, named after it (such as `Ex 13.1`), and do not change the queries, relationships, or pages the tutorials created. When an exercise needs a Table the tutorials trimmed or filtered, import it again under the query name the exercise gives. Turn off **Auto date/time** and the autodetection of relationships in the copy, as in Tutorial 13.1, if your copy does not already have them off.

### Financial Accounting Exercises

**Exercise 13.1: Revenue Control Totals by Year and Item Group**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item table from Master Data

**Scenario.** Before the report is shared, the controller wants a second set of control totals on the Validation page: revenue by item group for each fiscal year, and proof that the invoice lines add up to the invoices they belong to.

**Requirements.**

(1) Build a matrix with FiscalYear on rows, ItemGroup on columns, and LineTotal as values, with row and column totals. Compare the fiscal 2026 column totals with the revenue by item group you calculated in Chapter 6.

(2) Import T16_SalesInvoice again as a query named `InvoiceHeaders`, keep SalesInvoiceID, InvoiceDate, SubTotal, FreightAmount, TaxAmount, and GrandTotal, and add a FiscalYear custom column. Before you choose the columns, make sure FreightAmount has the decimal number type, as Discount does in Step 3 of Tutorial 13.1. Do not relate it to the other tables. Build a table visual of SubTotal by fiscal year from InvoiceHeaders, and compare it with the line totals by fiscal year.

(3) Add FreightAmount, TaxAmount, and GrandTotal to the table visual. Explain why the line totals reconcile to SubTotal but not to GrandTotal, and which of the four amounts is revenue from the sale of goods and services.

(4) Explain why InvoiceHeaders should not be related to SalesInvoiceLine in this model, given that SalesInvoice already is.

**Deliverable.** The matrix and the table visual on the Ex 13.1 page, with a short note of the comparisons.




**Exercise 13.2: Customer Concentration by Name or by Key**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Customer table from Master Data

**Scenario.** The controller is preparing a note on customer concentration for the audit committee and asks which customers produced the most revenue in fiscal 2026 and what share the largest ten held. Company policy treats any customer above 5% of annual revenue as a concentration to be reported.

**Requirements.**

(1) Build a table visual of CustomerName and LineTotal for fiscal 2026, sorted from the largest, and filtered to the top 10 customers with the **Top N** filter type in the Filters pane.

(2) Build a second table visual with CustomerID, CustomerName, and LineTotal, with the same filter. Compare the two lists and explain any difference.

(3) Find every customer name that belongs to more than one CustomerID, and state how much revenue each of those customers produced in fiscal 2026.

(4) Calculate the share of fiscal 2026 revenue held by the largest customer and by the top ten, and state whether any customer reaches the policy's threshold.

(5) Explain why the Top N filter belongs on the page, where the reader can see it, or in the visual's title, and write the title you would give the corrected visual.

**Deliverable.** Two table visuals and a half-page note to the controller.




### Managerial Accounting Exercises

**Exercise 13.3: Promotions in the Report**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item table from Master Data

**Scenario.** The marketing manager asks for the promotions to appear in the report by name, with what each one gave away, month by month, so that the 2027 calendar can be discussed with the facts on the page.

**Requirements.**

(1) Import T7_PromotionProgram as a query named `PromotionProgram`, keep PromotionID, PromotionCode, PromotionName, ScopeType, DiscountPct, EffectiveStartDate, and EffectiveEndDate, and relate it to SalesInvoiceLine on PromotionID.

(2) Build a matrix with PromotionName on rows, Month on columns, and DiscountAmount and the count of SalesInvoiceLineID as values, for fiscal 2026. Explain the row labeled (Blank): what it holds, and whether it signals a problem.

(3) Add EffectiveStartDate and EffectiveEndDate to the rows, and identify, for each promotion with lines in fiscal 2026, the months in which lines were invoiced after the promotion's end date. Recall what Chapter 5 found about the orders behind those lines.

(4) One promotion's end date is earlier than its start date. Identify it, and explain how its invoice lines can still carry the promotion.

(5) Write a short memo to the marketing manager stating what the promotions of fiscal 2026 gave away, when, and on which item groups, and what the report cannot yet show about whether they paid off.

**Deliverable.** The matrix on the Ex 13.3 page and a half-page memo.




**Exercise 13.4: A Page for the Sales Manager**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Customer table from Master Data

**Scenario.** The sales manager wants a page for the sales team: revenue by customer segment and region, the discounts each segment received, and the ability to look at one region at a time. The manager reads the page in two ways: in meetings, to see at a glance which segments and regions matter most, and on calls with the regional representatives, to quote exact figures.

**Requirements.**

(1) Using the theory of cognitive fit, decide which visual serves each of the manager's two tasks, and explain your choice in two or three sentences.

(2) Build the page for fiscal 2026: a clustered bar chart of revenue by segment, sorted from the largest, a matrix of revenue by segment and region with totals, and a card of discounts by segment. Add a slicer for Region that the manager can see.

(3) Click each segment's bar in turn and describe what happens to the matrix and the card. Then use **Format > Edit interactions** so that the bar chart filters the card but leaves the matrix unchanged, and explain when that behavior is preferable.

(4) Explain why the region restriction belongs in a slicer rather than in the **Filters on this page** section, and name one restriction that would belong in the Filters pane instead.

(5) Add a title to each visual that states what it shows and for which period, and alternative text to the bar chart.

**Deliverable.** The Ex 13.4 page and a short note on your design choices.




### Auditing Exercises

**Exercise 13.5: Profiling the Sales Tables on the Entire Data Set**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item and Customer tables from Master Data

**Scenario.** An internal auditor reviewing the report asks you to document a profile of the four source Tables before anyone relies on the report, and to show how much the profile depends on the rows it is based on.

**Requirements.**

(1) Import T17_SalesInvoiceLine, T16_SalesInvoice, T44_Item, and T4_Customer again as queries named `Profile_Lines`, `Profile_Invoices`, `Profile_Items`, and `Profile_Customers`, with every column. Correct Discount in Profile_Lines and FreightAmount in Profile_Invoices to the decimal number type, as in Step 3 of Tutorial 13.1. Clear **Enable load** on each, so that they stay in the Power Query Editor and do not enter the model.

(2) With **Column quality**, **Column distribution**, and **Column profile** turned on, record for each query, on the top 1,000 rows, the share of empty values in every column that has any, and the number of distinct values of PricingMethod, Discount, and Status.

(3) Switch to the entire data set and record the same figures. Identify every column whose profile changes materially, and explain why the first 1,000 rows of these Tables are not representative.

(4) For three of the columns with empty values, decide whether the blanks are meaningful blanks (Chapter 5), data that should exist, or a matter for follow-up, and give your reason.

(5) Write a one-page profile memo, in the form of Chapter 10's data profile, that the auditor can file with the report.

**Deliverable.** A one-page profile memo with the two sets of figures.




**Exercise 13.6: Reviewing a Draft Report Page**

**Table group:** Order-to-Cash, with the Item and Customer tables from Master Data

**Scenario.** A colleague has drafted a page for the board. It has a pie chart of fiscal 2026 revenue by item group with five slices and no labels, a card titled "Average discount" showing Average of Discount for fiscal 2026, a line chart of revenue by month from January 2024 to December 2026 on the default axis, a line and clustered column chart of revenue and discounts by month of fiscal 2026, and, on that chart only, a filter in the Filters pane that excludes the Services item group, mentioned nowhere on the page. The controller asks you to review it before it goes out.

**Requirements.**

(1) Rebuild the draft page in your copy of the report, exactly as described, on a page named `Ex 13.6 Draft`.

(2) For each element, write a review note that states what a reader would conclude, why that conclusion is wrong or unsupported, and what the correct figure or picture is. Use the figures in your report to support each note.

(3) Build a corrected page, `Ex 13.6 Revised`, that replaces each element with an honest equivalent. For the average discount, state what the card should show instead and why the report cannot yet calculate it correctly.

(4) Apply the accessibility practices of this chapter to the revised page, and list what you changed.

**Deliverable.** The two pages and a set of review notes, one for each element of the draft.
